land.text: the same kingdom under its earlier Cliopatria name: the Kingdom of Scotland page dates it 'traditionally said to have been founded in 843' and gives one infobox 843-1707; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba row ends in 1293

predecessors.note: Rule 2: one state, one colour. The researcher treats Alba (900-1293) and Scotland (1294-1707) as a single kingdom split only by Cliopatria's naming; see notes.

land.text: 'political union with England as the Kingdom of Great Britain, which came into force on 1 May 1707'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Great Britain begins in 1709; its Kingdom of England row already carries Scotland in 1706-1708.

capitals.name: Edinburgh
capitals.note: Infobox: Edinburgh (after c. 1452); the page says it 'developed as a capital city in the second half of the 15th century'. In July 1651 the Third English Civil War page calls Perth 'the seat of the Scottish government'.

minus.text: the Isle of Man, English from 1290 to 1313

correction.text: the 1294 shape without the Isle of Man: 'In 1290, King Edward I of England sent Walter de Huntercombe to take possession of Man'

keyframe_review.note: 86,071 km2 against the infobox's 78,778 km2 (1482-1707): ratio 1.09, fine for a shape that still holds the Isle of Man. The Isle of Man page has Edward I send Walter de Huntercombe 'to take possession of Man' in 1290, and 'It remained in English hands until 1313', so the island's two cells are removed. Orkney and Shetland (Norwegian until 1468-1472) are correctly absent. The shape stands for 1294-1304 although Scotland was invaded and its king deposed in 1296 (occupation events in the ledger; Cliopatria draws no gap until 1305).

correction.text: Scotland under English occupation: 'a parliament was held in May 1305' with the English holding real power; Bruce crowned 25 March 1306; 'The Battle of Bannockburn in 1314 was an especially important Scottish victory'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria leaves blank (1305-1313). The First War page has Edward I's English government over Scotland in 1305 ('Edward in effect ruler of Scotland' since July 1296), Robert Bruce crowned at Scone on 25 March 1306, forced out of the mainland after Methven, back in 1307, and Bannockburn in 1314 ending the English occupation. The page does not say what Bruce held year by year, so the shape is all of Scotland, drawn as occupied land (ledger occupation events 1304-1314) with the Bruce kingdom as the state it belongs to.

minus.text: the Isle of Man, Scottish only 1313-1314 and 1317-1333

correction.text: the 1314 shape without the Isle of Man, which the ledger adds back for 1317-1333

keyframe_review.note: Same 86,071 km2 shape for 1314-1474. The Isle of Man page: Bruce took Man in 1313, English retook it in 1314, the Scots in 1317, 'held by the Scots until 1333', then back and forth 'until the English took it for the last time in 1346'. The island is therefore taken out of the baseline and carried by the ledger (gain 1313, loss 1314, gain 1317, loss 1333, contest 1333-1346). Berwick (sacked in March 1296, fell to the Scots in 1318 per the page, English again in 1482) lies outside the shape's cells at this resolution and is carried by ledger events. One 253 km2 cell in Northumberland at 55.32N 2.46W is border simplification, left in. Orkney and Shetland are correctly absent until 1472; the Lords of the Isles held the Hebrides as a 'functionally independent' lordship until 1493.

88,868 km2 (infobox 78,778 km2 for 1482-1707, ratio 1.13): the shape adds Orkney and Shetland (8 grid cells, 2,023 km2), annexed in 1471 (Northern Isles page) or 1472 (Kingdom of Scotland page: 'in 1266 and 1472 respectively'), after Shetland was pledged in 1468 as security for the dowry of Margaret. The Isle of Man is gone, as it should be. Berwick, English again from 1482, is not in the cells.

minus.text: Northern Ireland, which no page opened gives to the Scottish crown

correction.text: the 1552 shape without its Irish cells; the Debatable Lands division is carried by the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 90,185 km2 (ratio 1.14 to the infobox) but the five cells added in 1552 lie on the County Down and Antrim coast of Ireland (54.36-54.73N, 5.65-6.0W), not on the Debatable Lands. The 1552 date matches the Debatable Lands partition ('In 1552, commissioners from Scotland and England met and divided the Debatable Lands between England and Scotland', the Scots' Dike running from the Esk to the Sark), but that land lies on the Solway border and is already inside the Natural Earth Scotland polygon. No page opened has Scotland holding land in Ireland, so the Northern Ireland cells are removed.

correction.text: the 1556 shape without its Irish cells

keyframe_review.note: 91,923 km2: seven more cells on the Antrim and Down coast (up to 55.21N, 6.37W), again Irish land that no page gives to Scotland. Same correction as 1552.

correction.text: the 1579 shape without its Irish cells

keyframe_review.note: 92,365 km2 (ratio 1.17): two more Down cells (54.21N, 5.97W and 54.83N, 6.34W). Same correction as 1552; the Scottish-Irish cells are the only growth between 1475 and 1608, and no page opened dates any Scottish gain after 1552.

correction.text: the 1602 shape without its Irish cells

keyframe_review.note: Same 92,365 km2 shape for 1602-1608 with the same Irish cells; the Union of the Crowns of 1603 ('In 1603, James VI of Scotland became King of England, forming a personal union') leaves Scotland a separate kingdom. Same correction as 1552.

correction.text: Scotland as its own kingdom: 'a personal union between Scotland and England' from 1603, until the union 'with England as the Kingdom of Great Britain, which came into force on 1 May 1707'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1609-1706, the years Cliopatria folds Scotland into its Kingdom of England row (341,650 km2 in 1609-1639, 341,939 km2 in 1662-1690, 341,676 km2 in 1691-1705). The Kingdom of Scotland page says the 1603 union was 'a personal union between Scotland and England' and gives the kingdom's end as the Acts of Union, in force on 1 May 1707, so Scotland remains a state of its own, with its own Parliament, until then. The Commonwealth's conquest (1652) and the Restoration (1660) are ledger events. Infobox area 78,778 km2 (1482-1707) against the Natural Earth Scotland of 83,457 km2 on the grid.

region.text: Scotland as Cliopatria draws it in 1294, without the Isle of Man

ledger.note: 1294: the Kingdom of Scotland (Cliopatria's name for the kingdom of Alba from 1294). Page silent on 1294: the Kingdom of Scotland infobox gives 'traditionally founded 843' and its end in 1707; the row begins here only because the kingdom-of-alba row ends in 1293.

region.text: the western seaboard and islands under the Lords of the Isles

ledger.note: Page silent on the start: the Hebrides came to Scotland by the 1266 Treaty of Perth (Kingdom of Scotland page) but 'Successive Lords of the Isles fiercely asserted their independence from Scotland' and 'the island chiefs remained functionally independent for many centuries' (Lordship of the Isles page). Drawn as a lighter tint inside the Scottish shape until the 1493 forfeiture.

region.text: Berwick-upon-Tweed and Dunbar in East Lothian

ledger.note: 1296: Edward I invades Scotland. 'That same month, Edward invaded Scotland and stormed Berwick-upon-Tweed' (March 1296); Balliol's army was 'overwhelmingly defeated at the Battle of Dunbar' in April.
1296: Balliol is deposed. 'By July, John was deposed as king and sent into exile'; over 1,800 Scottish nobles swore homage, leaving Edward in effect ruler of Scotland.
1296: England occupies Scotland (July). 'By July, John was deposed as king and sent into exile', with Edward 'in effect ruler of Scotland'.

region.text: Scotland, cleared by Moray and Wallace

ledger.note: 1297: the Scots clear the English out after Stirling Bridge (11 September), leaving only Dundee Castle in English hands. 'On 11 September 1297, Scottish forces, under the joint command of Moray and Wallace' defeated Surrey at Stirling Bridge.

region.text: Scotland, the campaigns of Edward I 1298-1303

ledger.note: 1298: Edward I returns and beats Wallace at Falkirk (22 July). 'On 22 July, Edward's army attacked a much smaller Scottish force led by Wallace'; he 'invaded Scotland' on 3 July 1298 but returned without fully subduing it. Campaigns and truces follow in 1300, 1301, 1302 and 1303.

1304: the Scots submit. 'Terms of submission were negotiated on 9 February by John Comyn' and 'all the leading Scots surrendered to Edward in February'; Stirling Castle fell after a siege of about three months.

1304: England again rules Scotland. After the February submission 'a parliament was held in May 1305' with the English holding real power and the Earl of Richmond in Roxburgh and Jedburgh castles; this is the interval Cliopatria leaves blank (1305-1313).

1306: Robert Bruce is crowned King of Scots at Scone (25 March). 'At Scone Abbey on 25 March 1306, Robert Bruce was crowned as King Robert I of Scotland': the Balliol line gives way to the Bruce line, same kingdom and colour.
1313: Bruce takes the Isle of Man. 'It remained in English hands until 1313, when Robert the Bruce of Scotland took it' after a siege of Castle Rushen.
1314: Bannockburn ends the English occupation. 'The Battle of Bannockburn in 1314 was an especially important Scottish victory'; the page puts de facto independence in 1314 (it gives no day).
1314: the English retake the Isle of Man. 'In 1314, it was retaken for the English by John Bacach of Argyll.'
1317: the Scots retake the Isle of Man. 'In 1317, it was retaken for the Scots by Thomas Randolph, 1st Earl of Moray.'

region.text: Berwick and the north of England raided by Bruce

ledger.note: 1318: Berwick falls and the Borders war begins. 'They were also crucial in the blockade of Berwick, which led to its fall in 1318.' Bruce's invasion of northern England followed until the 1328 treaty.
1318: the Scots take Berwick. 'the blockade of Berwick, which led to its fall in 1318'.
1328: the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton recognises Scottish independence (1 May). Bruce's invasion of northern England forced the English 'on 1 May 1328' to sign it.

region.text: the Isle of Man, held by the Scots until 1333

ledger.note: 1333: the Scots lose the Isle of Man. 'It was held by the Scots until 1333.' The page does not say to whom it passed in that year.
1333: the island passes back and forth. 'control passed back and forth between the two kingdoms until the English took it for the last time in 1346.' The page gives no more dates.
1346: the English take the Isle of Man for the last time. '...until the English took it for the last time in 1346.'
1452: the capital moves from Dunfermline to Edinburgh. Infobox: Dunfermline (c. 1069-1452), Edinburgh (after c. 1452).

region.text: Orkney and Shetland, from the Norwegian crown

ledger.note: 1472: Scotland annexes Orkney and Shetland. 'The dowry of the Orkney and Shetland Islands, by the Norwegian crown, in 1468' was Scotland's last major land acquisition; the annexation of the Northern Isles came 'in 1472' (Northern Isles page: pledged by Christian I in 1468, 'the following year' after the 1470 cession 'directly annexed', i.e. 1471).
1482: Berwick falls to the English for the last time. 'In 1482 the border fortress of Berwick - the largest port in medieval Scotland - fell to the English once again.'

region.text: the Hebrides and the Lords' mainland holdings

ledger.note: 1493: the Lordship of the Isles is forfeit. 'Upon the discovery of his alliance with Edward IV in 1493... The end of the MacDonald Lords came in 1493 when John MacDonald II...'; the Hebrides pass under the Crown's direct rule.

region.text: the Debatable Lands from the Solway Firth near Carlisle to Langholm, with Canonbie

ledger.note: 1552: the Debatable Lands are divided. 'In 1552, commissioners from Scotland and England met and divided the Debatable Lands between England and Scotland', the Scots' Dike running from the Esk to the Sark: the end of the territory's 'de facto independence'. The page does not say which side received which part, so the region is the whole strip (about ten miles by four, Solway Firth to Langholm).
1650: Cromwell invades Scotland (22 July). 'On 22 July the New Model Army under Oliver Cromwell invaded Scotland' and beat the Scots at Dunbar on 3 September.

region.text: Perth, Stirling, Alyth, St Andrews and Dundee, taken between July and 1 September 1651

ledger.note: 1651: the central Lowlands fall to the Commonwealth. Perth was marched on on 31 July 1651; 'By the end of August, Monck had captured Stirling, Alyth, and St Andrews'; 'the English stormed the west and east ports' of Dundee on 1 September 1651. The page names towns, not provinces: the region is the researcher's reading.

1652: the last Scottish strongholds surrender. Dunnottar Castle 'was the last major Scottish stronghold to surrender, on 24 May 1652'; the Third English Civil War page dates Worcester to 3 September 1651, 'marking the end of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms'.

region.text: Scotland, incorporated in the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland

ledger.note: 1652: Scotland is conquered and, from 1653, incorporated in the Commonwealth. The page: 'the short-lived incorporation of Scotland into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland (1653-1660)'; the Ordinance for uniting Scotland with England was issued on 12 April 1654 (Commonwealth dossier).

region.text: Scotland, restored to its own kingdom

ledger.note: 1660: Scotland leaves the Commonwealth with the Restoration of Charles II. The page ends the 'incorporation of Scotland into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland' in 1660 and gives no month.

region.text: Scotland, entering the Kingdom of Great Britain

ledger.note: 1707: the Kingdom of Scotland unites with England as Great Britain (1 May). 'Political union with England as the Kingdom of Great Britain, which came into force on 1 May 1707.'

wars.name: First War of Scottish Independence
wars.outcome: Scottish victory: Balliol deposed 1296, Stirling Bridge 1297, Falkirk 1298, submission 1304, Bruce crowned 1306, Bannockburn 1314, and the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton of 1 May 1328 recognises independence.
wars.note: The page gives no date for Bannockburn's day, Perth 1313, Roxburgh or Edinburgh 1314, or Berwick 1318.

wars.name: Struggle for the Isle of Man
wars.outcome: The island changed hands in 1313 (Scots), 1314 (English), 1317 (Scots), 1333 (English, then 'back and forth') and passed to the English 'for the last time in 1346'.

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish War (Third English Civil War)
wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory: Dunbar (3 September 1650), Worcester (3 September 1651), Dundee (1 September 1651), Dunnottar (24 May 1652); Scotland incorporated in the Commonwealth.

certainty.note: War, occupation and reconquest; the English border moved with Berwick and the Borders campaigns.

The border with England was fixed 'close to the modern border' by the Treaty of York (1237); exceptions: Berwick (changing hands, English again in 1482), the Debatable Lands (no border until 1552) and the Hebrides under the Lords of the Isles (soft until 1493).
The Scots' Dike of 1552 closes the last undefined stretch of the English border; Orkney and Shetland are island coasts. Soft only for the Commonwealth conquest 1650-1652.

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from the pages listed (six pages for the Scottish story; the Isle of Man page belongs to the Isle of Man dossier's budget).

DECISIONS FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR
1. Life span. Cliopatria's row is 1294-1608 and its Kingdom of Alba row is 900-1293, but the Kingdom of Scotland page gives one kingdom 843-1707. The dossier starts at 1294 (found, confidence 1, page silent) and ends on 1 May 1707 (page, confidence 3), with a new keyframe 1609-1706 (Scotland as its own kingdom in personal union). Cliopatria folds Scotland into its Kingdom of England row from 1609 (341,650 km2 for 1609-1639; 341,939 km2 for 1662-1690; and 1706-1708), so the kingdom-of-england dossier (another part of eu-11) may also draw Scotland: if both are drawn, Scotland is doubled in 1609-1639 and 1662-1706. The England dossier should subtract Scotland or the renderers should prefer this dossier there. Rule 2: kingdom-of-alba and this dossier are one kingdom, one colour; kingdom-of-alba should be a `rename` predecessor.
2. Irish cells. The 1552, 1556, 1579 and 1602 shapes carry 5, 12, 14 and 14 grid cells on the County Down and Antrim coast. No page opened gives any Irish land to the Scottish crown, so each shape is 'adjust' with Northern Ireland subtracted. Cliopatria probably drew the MacDonnell Scots settlement of Antrim; a gap-filler may check.
3. Isle of Man. The 1294-1304 and 1314-1474 shapes include the island (2 cells). The Isle of Man page has it English 1290-1313, Scottish 1313-1314 and 1317-1333, contested to 1346. Shapes are 'adjust' (island removed); the ledger carries the gains and losses.
4. Gap 1305-1313. Cliopatria has no Scotland; the pages give no territory for Bruce's kingdom year by year (Methven, forced out of the mainland, back in 1307), so the new keyframe is all of Scotland drawn as English-occupied (occupation events 1304-1314) with the Bruce kingdom owning it. The Bruce Irish campaign and Edward Bruce's crowning are not on the First War page and are not recorded.

NOT SETTLED (pages silent): the Hebrides as a vassal from 1294 (vassal_start is confidence 1, only the 1493 end is dated); Berwick between 1318 and 1482 (the 1333 loss and the 1461 recovery are not on the pages opened); which half of the Debatable Lands went to Scotland (the page does not say); the date of the Union of the Crowns' effect on the border; rulers (no list opened, `rulers` omitted).
Matching losses expected in the kingdom-of-england dossier: the Isle of Man (1313, 1317), Berwick (1318, and its 1482 gain). Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-alba (other part of eu-11, 900-1293), Lordship of the Isles (name only; years from the pages: ended 1493; founding date not on the pages; eu-11-x), kingdom-of-great-britain, kalmar-union (Norwegian crown 1468-72; eu-14), kingdom-of-england, commonwealth-of-england (mine).
Gazetteer: no new names needed except the Debatable Lands (used lon/lat 55.05N 2.95W, 12 km) and, if wanted, Canonbie.
